name: Order and execution
description: How a customer gets a price, accepts it, and has the resulting trade settled and told to them. Does not cover onboarding, funding or reporting — those are separate packs.

processes.name: Order and execution
processes.description: A customer converts one asset into another at a price the platform is willing to honour, and both sides of the exchange are recorded so the books balance.
processes.outcome: The trade is settled, the balance has moved, and the customer has been told.

processes.name: Getting estimate
processes.description: Working out what the customer would get, and whether they are allowed to have it, before anything is committed. Nothing here changes state — an abandoned estimate leaves no trace.
processes.trigger: The customer enters an amount in the app.
processes.outcome: A priced, validated estimate the customer can accept, or a refusal with a reason.

processes.name: Take the quote from the cache
processes.description: The local Redis copy answers almost every estimate. It is what keeps pricing fast when the market is moving and every customer is asking at once.

processes.name: Get prices from the pricing service
processes.description: Only on a cache miss or a stale quote. Pricing holds the reference rates and is the authority when the cache cannot answer.

processes.name: Check the customer may trade
processes.description: Reads the KYC state. A customer who has not passed verification is refused here rather than after they have accepted, so the refusal is fast and explainable.

processes.name: Check the balance covers it
processes.description: Reads the live wallet balance. This is a check, not a reservation — the funds only move once the order matches, so an estimate can still fail later if the balance moves underneath it.

processes.name: Accepting estimate and placing order
processes.description: The customer commits. From here the platform owns the outcome, so everything is written down before it is announced.
processes.outcome: The order is durably recorded and the matching engine has it.

processes.name: Receive the accepted order
processes.description: The gateway terminates the customer session and forwards the order; from here on the customer id is trusted and not re-checked.

processes.name: Persist the order
processes.description: Written as PENDING before anything is published, so a crash between here and the publish leaves a recoverable record rather than a lost order.

processes.name: Publish the order
processes.description: Keyed by instrument so one instrument's orders stay in sequence on a single partition. This publish is the handover: once it succeeds, order-service is no longer responsible for the outcome.

processes.name: Pick the order up for matching
processes.description: The matching engine holds its book in memory; this consume is how an order enters it.

processes.name: Matching and settlement
processes.description: Turning a resting order into an executed trade, and moving the money so the books and the customer's balance agree.
processes.trigger: An order enters the book, or a price tick moves it.
processes.outcome: Balanced postings exist and the customer's visible balance reflects the trade.

processes.name: Keep the book priced
processes.description: Market ticks continuously reprice the resting book, so a match can happen with no new order involved at all.

processes.name: Publish the fill
processes.description: One event per fill. A large order that fills in parts produces several, all carrying the same order id.

handsOffTo.note: The ledger posts the trade from the fill event.
Reporting ingests the fill off the topic to build the trade warehouse.

processes.name: Post the trade to the ledger
processes.description: Both legs written in one transaction, keyed on the fill id, so a redelivered event is a no-op rather than a double posting. This is the point the trade becomes real for accounting.

processes.name: Move the customer balance
processes.description: Updates the wallet the customer actually sees. Independent of the ledger posting, so the two can briefly disagree under load.

processes.name: Announce the new balance
processes.description: Carries the balance after the change, not the delta, so a consumer that missed an earlier event still ends up correct.

handsOffTo.note: Growth picks the balance change up and decides whether to tell the customer.

processes.name: Telling the customer
processes.description: Getting the fill in front of the customer, through whichever channel they have enabled. Best-effort throughout: a failure here never blocks the trade, which has already settled.
processes.outcome: The customer has been told, or the failure has been logged and dropped.

processes.name: Send the message
processes.description: Channel and locale come from the customer's notification preferences. A hard bounce is logged and not retried.
